Decide on Friend.GameId: either restore the mapping at Friend.cs:45 or remove the dead property if 'currently in-game' info is unused.

result.feature: Cross-cutting: security posture, dead code, and test suites
result.summary: The security baseline is genuinely solid: Program.cs registers a global authorization FallbackPolicy (RequireAuthenticatedUser) so every endpoint is authn-by-default, the Identity cookie is hardened (HttpOnly/SameSite/SlidingExpiry), an antiforgery header name is configured for AJAX, and /health is correctly AllowAnonymous. The previously-orphaned views (Views/Authentication, Views/User) and JS (hideGame.js, sum.js, qr.js) have actually been deleted. NUnit is real and green (84 passed, 0 skipped; UnitTest1.cs is now a genuine GapProcessorTests with assertions). BDD step defs assert real behavior via FluentAssertions + Selenium page objects. BUT three real gaps remain: (1) antiforgery is NOT global — only the 3 API ControllerBase controllers have it, so CompeteController's two [HttpPost] MVC actions are CSRF-vulnerable (and Initiate is self-documented as broken); (2) the JS test suite FAILS — sum_wwroot.test.js imports the deleted wwwroot/js/sum.js; (3) utils.js escapeHtml is dead code (never imported by any app JS), while the real XSS surface (Messages.js/competeCreatePage.js/achievements.js innerHTML interpolation) goes unescaped; plus an orphan CalculatorStepDefinitions.cs full of PendingStepException with no matching feature.

gaps.title: Antiforgery is not global; CompeteController POST actions are CSRF-vulnerable
gaps.detail: Program.cs registers a global FallbackPolicy for authentication but never registers a global AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute MVC filter. Antiforgery is only applied per-controller on SteamController.cs:15, MessagesController.cs:15, VoteController.cs:12, and explicitly on AdminController actions. CompeteController has [HttpPost] Initiate (line 404) and [HttpPost] Create (line 429) with no [ValidateAntiForgeryToken]/[AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken] at class or method level, so authenticated users can be CSRF'd into creating competitions. The E2E security.spec.js only checks antiforgery on /api/Steam/UpdateTheme, so this gap is untested.
gaps.fix: Register antiforgery globally in Program.cs: builder.Services.AddControllersWithViews(o => o.Filters.Add(new AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute())); This auto-validates all unsafe verbs while leaving GETs untouched. Then add an E2E case in security.spec.js POSTing to /Compete/Create without a token and asserting 400. (Initiate at line 404 is separately broken — see dead-code note — and should be removed or fixed before exposing it.)

gaps.title: JavaScript test suite fails: references deleted wwwroot/js/sum.js
gaps.detail: Running `npx jest` in src/Javascript_Tests yields: 1 failed, 1 passed. sum_wwroot.test.js does `import { sum } from '../../SteamProject/wwwroot/js/sum.js'` but wwwroot/js/sum.js was deleted during cleanup, so the suite fails with 'Cannot find module'. The package.json test script uses --passWithNoTests but that does not rescue an import error. So the JS test suite as a whole does NOT pass.
gaps.fix: Delete src/Javascript_Tests/tests/sum_wwroot.test.js (and the stray src/Javascript_Tests/tests/sum.js helper) since the production sum.js is gone. Keep utils.test.js. Verify with `npx jest` returning all green.

gaps.title: escapeHtml (utils.js) is dead code while real XSS surface is unescaped
gaps.detail: escapeHtml and the rest of utils.js are an ES module that is never imported by any app JS and never loaded via a <script> tag in any view (grep for 'utils' in Views/ and wwwroot/js/ returns nothing). It exists only to be exercised by utils.test.js. Meanwhile the actual rendering paths build DOM via innerHTML string interpolation with unescaped server/user data: Messages.js:59,145,155 (contact name/nickname/message), competeCreatePage.js:80,116 (steamName), achievements.js:80 (displayName). These are live stored-XSS vectors that escapeHtml was presumably meant to defend but does not.
gaps.fix: Either import escapeHtml into Messages.js/competeCreatePage.js/achievements.js and wrap every interpolated user/Steam-derived value (e.g. `${escapeHtml(contact.name)}`), or switch those to textContent/createElement. Then load utils.js as a module from the relevant views so it is no longer orphaned. If you choose textContent, delete utils.js + utils.test.js as dead code.

gaps.title: Orphan BDD CalculatorStepDefinitions full of PendingStepException
gaps.detail: CalculatorStepDefinitions.cs is the SpecFlow scaffolding template: all four steps (GivenTheFirstNumberIs, GivenTheSecondNumberIs, WhenTheTwoNumbersAreAdded, ThenTheResultShouldBe) throw new PendingStepException() with TODO comments. There is no Calculator.feature in BDD_Tests/Features, so these bindings are unreachable dead code. HelloWorldStepDefinitions.cs is also template scaffolding but at least has a real assertion and a matching HelloWorld.feature.
gaps.fix: Delete src/BDD_Tests/StepDefinitions/CalculatorStepDefinitions.cs. Optionally also remove the HelloWorld feature/steps if you do not want a placeholder smoke scenario in the suite.

gaps.title: InboxController returns a viewless View() and lacks explicit [Authorize]
gaps.detail: InboxController has no [Authorize] (relies on the global FallbackPolicy, which is OK) and no [AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken] (it has no POST actions, so OK). But Index() at line 30-34: if _userManager.GetUserId(User) is null it returns View() with no model, while line 37 returns View(userMessages) — the no-model branch will NRE in the .cshtml if it expects List<InboxMessage>. Under the FallbackPolicy an unauthenticated request is redirected before reaching the action, so the null branch is effectively dead, but it is a latent bug and misleading.
gaps.fix: Remove the dead null-id branch (the FallbackPolicy guarantees an authenticated user) or return RedirectToAction to login. Add [Authorize] explicitly for defense-in-depth/readability even though the fallback covers it.

gaps.title: E2E and BDD suites cannot self-run in plain CI (no auto-started web server)
gaps.detail: playwright.config.js has no `webServer` block; it assumes the app is already running at localhost:5105 (comment: 'the autonomous harness manages the dotnet process separately'). BDD's AppServerHooks.cs:18 auto-starts the app locally but explicitly skips startup when CI/GITHUB_ACTIONS is set, assuming a deployed app, and its scenarios require real Steam login + user-secrets (SeedUserPW) to pass. So neither browser suite is push-button runnable in a clean CI without external orchestration and secrets; only NUnit runs unattended.
gaps.fix: Add a `webServer` entry to playwright.config.js (command: 'dotnet run --project ../SteamProject', url: BASE_URL, reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI) so Playwright boots the app. For BDD, gate CI on a deployed URL via config and document required user-secrets, or mark Steam-dependent scenarios with a tag excluded in CI.
